title: About Handwashing

sections.heading: Why it's important
sections.text: Washing hands can keep you healthy and prevent the spread of respiratory and diarrheal infections. Germs can spread from person to person or from surfaces to people when you:

sections.heading: Why it's important
sections.text: Touch your eyes, nose, and mouth with unwashed hands

sections.heading: Why it's important
sections.text: Prepare or eat food and drinks with unwashed hands

sections.heading: Why it's important
sections.text: Touch surfaces or objects that have germs on them

sections.heading: Why it's important
sections.text: Blow your nose, cough, or sneeze into hands and then touch other people's hands or common objects

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: You can help yourself and your loved ones stay healthy by washing your hands often, especially during these key times when you are likely to get and spread germs:

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: Before, during, and after preparing food

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: Before and after eating food

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: Before and after caring for someone at home who is sick with vomiting or diarrhea

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: Before and after treating a cut or wound

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: After using the toilet

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: After changing diapers or cleaning up a child who has used the toilet

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: After blowing your nose, coughing, or sneezing

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: After touching an animal, animal feed, or animal waste

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: After handling pet food or pet treats

sections.heading: Key times to wash hands
sections.text: After touching garbage

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Washing your hands is easy, and it’s one of the most effective ways to prevent the spread of germs. Follow these five steps every time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Wet your hands with clean, running water (warm or cold), turn off the tap, and apply soap.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Lather your hands by rubbing them together with the soap. Lather the backs of your hands, between your fingers, and under your nails.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Scrub your hands for at least 20 seconds. Need a timer? Hum the “Happy Birthday” song from beginning to end twice.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Rinse your hands well under clean, running water.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Dry your hands using a clean towel or an air dryer.

sections.heading: Use hand sanitizer when you can't use soap and water
sections.text: Washing hands with soap and water is the best way to get rid of germs in most situations. If soap and water are not readily available, you can use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer that contains at least 60% alcohol. You can tell if the sanitizer contains at least 60% alcohol by looking at the product label.

sections.heading: What you can do
sections.text: CDC has health promotion materials to encourage kids and adults to make handwashing part of their everyday lives.

sections.heading: What you can do
sections.text: Share social media graphics and messages.

sections.heading: What you can do
sections.text: Print stickers and place clings on bathroom mirrors.

sections.heading: What you can do
sections.text: Promote handwashing on or around Global Handwashing Day, celebrated each year on October 15.

sections.heading: What you can do
sections.text: Distribute fact sheets to share information about hand hygiene for specific audiences.
